title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Top half (continuing the previous page, where equivalences Ens(π')→Ens(π) were identified with (π',π)-bitorsors): consider a (π,π)-bitorsor X together with an isomorphism μ: X∘X ≅ 1, where ∘ is contracted product. Such an 'involutive bitorsor' is an equivalence of the classifying topos Ens(π) with itself whose square is identified with the identity. The note 'λe = eλ ∀λ∈π' is most plausibly the coherence condition on μ. In extension language, for e∈X the element e² = μ(e,e) must commute with e (associativity μ(x,y)z = xμ(y,z)); as literally written it looks too strong (see errors). The claim is that the groupoid of such data ('Bi-inv(π)') is equivalent to the involutions of the 2-group of self-bitorsors of π (written 'Invol(End(π))', perhaps meaning the gr-category of bitorsors / Out-type data). This in turn is equivalent to the groupoid Ext(Z/2, π) of extensions 1→π→π̃→Z/2→1. The dictionary is π̃ = π ⊔ X, and X recovered as p^{-1}(1), the non-neutral coset. This is the Schreier/Breen description of extensions by a group Γ as monoidal functors Γ → Bitors(π), specialised to Γ = Z/2.

Bottom half: the motivating example. I is a finite (cyclically ordered) set of n ≥ 3 indices, and one considers 'cartes' (maps) attached to I. Define π_I = (Z/2)^{*I}, the free product of n involutions s_i. A struck-out attempt wrote π_I as L_I/(λ_0…λ_{n-1}=1). The final version takes the index-2 'orientation' subgroup π_I^+ of even words, giving 1→π_I^+→π_I→Z/2→1. Here π_I^+ ≅ L_I/(λ_0λ_1…λ_{n-1}) with λ_i = s_i s_{i+1}, which is the free group of rank n−1, i.e. π_1 of P^1 minus n real points. The quotient π_I is the orbifold group of the disk (upper half-plane) whose boundary is a mirror broken at n removed corners. Complex conjugation is the involutive bitorsor / Z/2-extension of the first half. S_I is noted as acting on π_I by permuting the generators.

The figure shows the geometric side: a surface tiled by quadrilaterals (n = 4) whose vertices are coloured 0,1,2,3. These are the lifts of the upper and lower half-planes, i.e. an n-coloured generalisation of Grothendieck's bicoloured maps/dessins, in an unoriented (real) version. Finite π_I-sets correspond to such tiled surfaces, possibly non-orientable. The next page carries this out for n = 4: presentation λ_3λ_2λ_1λ_0 = 1, ε² = 1, ελ_iε^{-1} = λ_i^{-1}, base points ±i swapped by conjugation. It then passes to the fundamental group π_1(X,Γ,a) of a space with group action, an extension of Γ.
errors: 'λe = eλ ∀λ∈π' read literally (every λ commuting with every e∈X) would force the outer action of Z/2 to be trivial. Presumably it is a coherence condition on μ (e.g. e·μ(e,e) = μ(e,e)·e), or it concerns only the 'symmetric' case; as written it is ambiguous or too strong.

The identification π_I^+ ≅ L_I/(λ_0⋯λ_{n-1}) uses a cyclic ordering of I (λ_i = s_i s_{i+1}). Hence the full S_I action on π_I does not respect this presentation; only the dihedral group of the cyclic order does. The note glosses this.
'Invol(End(π))' is probably a transcription/abbreviation issue: involutions should be taken in the 2-group of self-bitorsors (≈ Aut(π) with inner morphisms), not in the monoid End(π).

ideas.what: Involutive (π,π)-bitorsors with μ: X∘X≅1 are equivalent to extensions of Z/2 by π, with X = p^{-1}(nontrivial element)
ideas.modern_name: Schreier theory via bitorsors / monoidal functors Z/2 → Bitors(π)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier; Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971); Breen (Bitorseurs et cohomologie non abélienne, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor formalism is in SGA/Giraud circles; not seen in this form in Grothendieck's own texts

ideas.what: Equivalences of classifying topoi Ens(π)≃Ens(π) as bitorsors; real structure as an involution of the topos
ideas.modern_name: Morita theory of groups/topoi; descent for Gal(C/R)

ideas.what: π_I = (Z/2)^{*I}, with even subgroup π_I^+ ≅ free group L_I/(λ_0⋯λ_{n-1}) = π_1(P^1 − n real points), and the extension by complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of a polygon with mirror boundary; extended (real) fundamental group / unoriented cartographic group for n punctures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Coxeter-type free products); real dessins: Singerman, Köck–Singerman; n-point constellations: Lando–Zvonkin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the unoriented cartographic groups and Gal(C/R) for n=3, not this general-n free-product setup as far as known

ideas.what: Unoriented 'I-maps': surfaces tiled by n-gons with vertices coloured by I (figure for n=4), classified by finite (Z/2)^{*I}-sets
ideas.modern_name: Real/unoriented generalised dessins (constellations) for covers of P^1 branched over n real points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lando–Zvonkin (constellations); work on real dessins and hypermaps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse §§2–4 treat n=3 maps and combinatorial polyhedra

missed.claim: Grothendieck links the abstract bitorsor description of Z/2-extensions directly to the combinatorics of unoriented n-coloured maps. Complex conjugation on π_1(P^1 − n real points) is viewed as an involutive self-bitorsor, and the resulting extension is (Z/2)^{*I} = the group of the n-gon tiling. This generalises his 3-point unoriented cartographic group to n points with real branch locus.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean combinatorial model for real covers branched at n real points: tilings by n-gons with I-coloured vertices. It is relevant to real dessins and to the Gal(C/R) part of anabelian/Teichmüller-tower questions. The literature mostly treats n=3 or uses permutation constellations rather than this free-product/bitorsor viewpoint, but the content is largely known.

missed.claim: The S_I action on π_I and its compatibility with the extension (and with the presentation of π_I^+) is only indicated. A study of the S_I- or dihedral-equivariance of these 'I-cartes' (moduli of n real points) is not developed here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would connect to real moduli spaces M_{0,n}(R) and their tiling by associahedra/cyclic orders. Only a hint is present.

deep.surprise_reason: The bitorsor/extension equivalence is classical. The n-point unoriented generalisation of maps via (Z/2)^{*I}, with the quadrilateral-tiling figure, is a nice unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck extending the Esquisse cartographic picture to n real punctures. However, the mathematics itself is elementary and essentially present in later work on real dessins and constellations.
transcription_corrections: 'Bi-inv(π) ≅ Invol(End(π))': the second term likely reads 'Invol(Bit(π))' or similar (involutions in the gr-category of self-bitorsors); the image shows 'Invol( E... (π))'.
'p^{-1}(1) ↪ él. ...' probably reads 'p^{-1}(1) ↪ élément non neutre', i.e. 1 denotes the non-trivial element of Z/2, and X is recovered as that coset.
'I ... pol. combi. fini d'ordre n≥3' probably reads 'I ensemble fini [cycliquement ordonné / polygone combinatoire] d'ordre n ≥ 3'.
'cartes ... I-...' is likely 'cartes non orientées, I-polygonales' (or similar).
The figure has n = 4: quadrilaterals with vertices coloured 0,1,2,3, not triangles.
